expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: During the deployment window, the migration will drop the column while the old version of the code is still running and trying to read it

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: We must split the current PR into two separate deployments following the **Expand and Contract** pattern

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: dropping a column is an irreversible operation. If we need to roll back, reverting the code will not bring the column (or its data) back

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: Restoring from a backup could take hours... establish the exact time it would take to restore the database from backup if the column drop causes unforeseen issues

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: require staff who may be unavailable on a Friday afternoon... Deploy it next week during regular hours when full staffing is available

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: No mention of a CI gate or automated prevention mechanism

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: Do not merge and deploy the current PR as-is

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: This is a reversible change. If something breaks, we can easily roll back the code. (for PR 1)
